section.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on the known concept that every person who fulfills a mitzvah is called a tzaddik, the idea of transformation applies not only to complete tzaddikim but to all who perform mitzvos, as each mitzvah refines a specific detail of the body and animal soul.
section.t: And based on the known [concept]
that every single person
(even when he is on the level of a Beinoni, and even below a Beinoni)
who fulfills a mitzvah is called by the name "tzaddik"
[because the totality of mitzvos is called by the name "tzedakah" (charity/righteousness),
and therefore the one who fulfills the mitzvos is called by the name "tzaddik" after the name of tzedakah
(mitzvos)],
it must be said,
that the matter of transformation is not only regarding tzaddikim in their simple sense, but also regarding those who fulfill mitzvos in general.
For since the mitzvos were only given to refine the creations through them
(refinement, from the term clarification and purification),
and each time a person fulfills a mitzvah, a particular detail of the body and the animal soul is clarified,
behold, regarding this particular detail that has been clarified, he is already in the category of tzaddik,
transformation.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This is connected to the distinction between Pesach and the counting of the Omer, where the work of Nissan is subjugation of evil and the work of Iyar is transformation, as explained regarding the difference between the first and second Pesach.
section.t: And it is possible to connect this with what is explained in the maamar "Lehavin Inyan Pesach Sheni"
(of the Tzemach Tzedek),
that the difference between the first Pesach and the second Pesach corresponds to the difference between the month of Nissan and the month of Iyar.
That the service of the month of Nissan,
whose matter is the Exodus from Egypt,
is the service of "turn away from evil,"
meaning that the evil is in its full strength and the service is to turn away from evil,
to go out and flee from evil,
subjugation.
And the service of the month of Iyar is the service of transformation.
And as is explained in Likkutei Torah
in the explanation of the verse
"On the first of the second month... of their going out from the land of Egypt,"
that the first service of the Exodus from Egypt,
the first month,
is subjugation of the sitra achra,
and after this comes a second service in the Exodus from Egypt,
the second month,
transformation.
And this is that the unique matter of the month of Iyar is the Counting of the Omer,
whose matter is
the clarification of the midos and their transformation into holiness,
transformation.
And based on this, the maamar explains

the reason for this, that on the first Pesach chametz is forbidden under penalty of "bal yera'eh u'bal yimatzeh" (it shall not be seen nor found), and on the second Pesach chametz and matzah are together with him in the house,
because on the first Pesach,
when the midos are not yet clarified
(and the service then is only subjugation),
one must be extremely careful regarding evil — "bal yera'eh u'bal yimatzeh,"
and on the second Pesach
(Iyar),
when he has already gone out from evil
(transformation),
it is possible to clarify, refine, and elevate even the chametz.
[And it is noteworthy,
that similar to this is the distinction between tzaddikim
(transformation)
and baalei teshuvah
(subjugation),
that a tzaddik must say "I desire [it], but what can I do, for my Father in Heaven has decreed upon me,"
unlike a baal teshuvah who must say "I do not desire [it],"
for he needs extra vigilance.]
And from this it is proven that the matter of transformation applies also regarding a particular matter.
For the second Pesach is in the middle of the days of the counting, and there still remain midos that need to be clarified,
and nevertheless the maamar says that on the second Pesach there is the matter of transformation,
because regarding the midos that were clarified in the days before the second Pesach, he has already gone out from evil,
transformation.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The reason the Exodus was through subjugation and the Omer through transformation is that the Exodus was an arousal from above, which does not penetrate internally, while the Omer is man's service, an arousal from below that draws down a revelation internally, affecting even the animal soul.
section.t: And now, the reason for this, that the Exodus from Egypt was in a manner of subjugation and the Counting of the Omer is in a manner of transformation,
is,
because the Exodus from Egypt was from the side of an arousal from above,
and the revelation drawn down from above
(not through man's service)
is not drawn into the interior so much,
and the Counting of the Omer is man's service,
an arousal from below,
and the revelation drawn down from above through man's service
[an arousal from above that comes through an arousal from below]
is internal.
And although the revelation that comes from above is more elevated than the revelation drawn down through man's service
[for a created being through his service can only reach his own root],
and so too it is regarding the Exodus from Egypt and the Counting of the Omer,
that the revelation that was at the Exodus from Egypt was that the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, was revealed to them in His very glory,
and the month of Iyar is called the month of "Ziv" (splendor)
because the revelation drawn down in this month is only a radiance
[And it must be said,
that in addition to this, that the revelation drawn down through man's service is lower than the revelation drawn down in the manner of an arousal from above by itself,
regarding the revelation drawn down through the service of the Counting of the Omer, it is even more so.
For since the service of the Counting of the Omer is
(preparation and)
before the Giving of the Torah,
therefore,
the revelation drawn down through the service of the Counting of the Omer is analogous to the revelation through the service of the Patriarchs before the Giving of the Torah
(when there was a decree and partition between the upper and lower realms)
which is lower than the revelation drawn down through service after the Giving of the Torah
(even though also the revelation drawn down through an arousal from below now is lower than the revelation drawn down from above by itself).
And this is that the month of Iyar is called "Ziv" because in it were born the "Zivtanei Olam" (the splendors of the world)
which are the Patriarchs,
whose mitzvos were "fragrances" (not fully actualized)],
nevertheless,
regarding the person,
the revelation that comes from above is felt
(primarily)
only in the G-dly soul and is not felt in the animal soul,
and therefore the service through this revelation is only subjugation,
and through man's service, and particularly through the revelation drawn down through service,
the clarification of the animal soul and its transformation into holiness is accomplished,
transformation.
